main_topics.reason: The user repeatedly asked whether their prescribed 2.4 g daily dose was correct or too low and ended by confirming the answer had cleared things up.
The user asked why formulation mattered and described taking twice-daily sachets, which the assistant used to contextualize the prescribed dose.
The user asked how long it would take to know whether the medication was working and received a timeframe and guidance on when to contact their gastroenterologist.
The user briefly asked whether to take the sachets with food.
The user mentioned their symptoms had been moderate when explaining the context for their new prescription.

output.summary: The user, recently diagnosed with ulcerative colitis, asked whether their prescribed mesalamine dose of 1.2 g twice daily was too low after the assistant initially gave 4.8 g as a typical dose without enough context. The assistant acknowledged that formulations and disease activity matter, answered follow-up questions about sachets, food, and when to expect an effect, and the user said they felt better and thanked it for clearing things up.
